usual_baseline: Oakland scoring is rarely used: 7.1% as a discharge criterion [2254]. Unstable patients seldom get CT angiography (0% [2248]; 4 of 6 with Shock Index >1 missed it [2654]). Inpatient endoscopy was 14.9% [2248]; 62.1% of major bleeds had no colonoscopy [2009]. Some unnecessary admissions and transfusions occur (14% and 7%) [2654].
fix_that_works: Teaching and BSG posters raised inpatient endoscopy from 14.9% to 66.7% and CT angiography in unstable patients from 0% to 50% [2248]. Posters and email raised DRE from 79% to 91% [2779]. Integrating BSG guidance cut 28-day readmission from 23.1% to 8.3%, with all discharges scoped [2500].
fix_that_fails: Oakland score documentation did not improve after posters and email; TXA use fell from 44% to 38% and CT-A from 29% to 19% [2779]. Oakland compliance improved minimally [2500]. After national guideline publication alone, Oakland use rose only to 14.6% [2254].
consultant_advice: Oakland score uptake stays low whatever the teaching. More useful is measuring safe discharge of minor bleeds, CT angiography in unstable patients and readmission. One site judged the Oakland score not accurate enough for safe discharge [2866], so pair scoring with outcome data.
